newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart, Limited sue Visa USA.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart, Limited sue Visa USA.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc and The Limited Inc have filed a class-action antitrust lawsuit against Visa USA Inc, alleging that retailers are being forced to accept a type of debit card for which they must pay "exorbitant" fees.

The suit, filed last week in a federal court in Brooklyn, seeks unspecified damages. It alleges retailers are paying hundreds of millions of dollars in fees. If the antitrust allegations were proven, that amount could be trebled.

The suit alleges that all retailers that accept the Visa credit card are being forced to accept Visa Check, a type of debit card that allows money from the customer's bank account to be transferred to the retailer.
Visa Check is described in the suit as being an "off-line" debit card, which electronically transfers money in one to five days after the sales transaction.
Off-line cards differ from "on-line" debit cards that allow the immediate transfer of money from customers accounts.

"Wal-Mart, The Limited and class members did not and do not want to accept Visa Check because the fees charged for Visa Check are exorbitant, fixed and maintained at supra-competitive levels only through the coercive force of the tying arrangement," the suit states.
The retailers allege that they are prohibited by Visa from asking customers if they would pay for their purchases by other debit cards such as NYCE or MAC, which charge retailers lower fees.

It alleges that in 1995 Visa Check cards were used in about 556 million retail transactions, comprising a dollar volume of about $22 billion. The interchange fees computed at the lowest possible rate for these transactions was about $250 million, the suit alleges.
Retailers would have paid less than $33 million in interchange fees for the same transactions processed by on-line debit networks, it alleges.
